clusters.name: Walter's move across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move with the family from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952, within the year: June became homesick and wrote to her sister Edna daily, then withdrew from Walter as he spent long hours in the orchard; Glen began fighting at his new school; Walter stopped writing to his brother Harlan after a quarrel over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that winter and then rowed with Walter over money for new trees. By September 1953, June had joined the church choir and her anxiety eased, marking where the family settled into the new place.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failed, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter began drinking heavily within weeks; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan and fell into conflict; Glen and Marian took over the family's finances and talks with the bank; Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; you began wetting the bed in April 1969; your grandmother Ida's heart trouble was found and she was told to stop working. Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning trees by October 1969, and Carl's asthma eased as spring came, marking where the family's crisis settled.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's job loss in February 1975 when the Ridgeport cannery closed: Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck in the yard; he and Marian fought loudly at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; you kept to your room and grew distant from your mother; your grandfather Walter began drinking again after six years sober. By March 1976 Glen started driving a delivery truck for the feed store, and by June you were eating again and made the track team, marking where the family's disruption settled.

clusters.name: Wilma moved into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into your house in January 1990 after selling her farm: you clashed with her over the children's bedtimes and meals; Hollis worked late and kept out of the rows; he took his mother's side; Owen began having tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; you developed eczema flaring on both hands; you and Hollis rowed most nights. When Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991, your eczema cleared over the summer, marking where the household conflict settled.
